title: Dick Bock's first recording session
summary: Dick Bock's first date with a trumpeter and five saxophones including Wardell Gray, featuring Edwards's 'Before Dawn'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And not too long after that, Dick Bock from Pacific Jazz and World Pacific Records, he did his first record date in the same little studio. He had a trumpet player named Louis Olsen(?) he brought from up north some place. And Wardell Gray and I worked the session with him. He had five saxophones and a trumpet and rhythm. And I wrote an arrangement for the group on one of my songs called "Before Dawn," for the five saxophones and the trumpet.
Around about 1947. This was Dick Bock's first venture in recording.
Oh yeah. He hadn't been involved with records at all. This was his first venture into recording.
Right. But he didn't even have a label at the time, I don't think. I don't remember. It didn't go far. It didn't go far. They pressed a few records, but it didn't go far.
No, I don't remember the name of the label that they were pressed on.
